newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes slide with WTI, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes slide with WTI, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices tracked the collapse in spot West Texas Intermediate (WTI) grade, but spot trade in Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude remained in unusual slump, traders said.
Market players said heavy Canadian imports, poor refining economics, and some earlier-than-expected maintenance work, have kept buyers at bay the last month.
Buyers said the current ANS differential of $2.30 a barrel under December WTI was satisfactory for their term contracts -- which are based on an ANS index.
Outright ANS prices slipped to $21.10/21.40, off 85 cents.

Traders on Wednesday said Celeron Trading and Transportation was the highest bidder in the U.S. government's offering of 15,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude from the Elk Hills Naval Petroleum Reserve in California today.
The company bid $22.078 a barrel for 4,165 bpd of crude from the 18G zone in Bakersfield, Calif. The prices was based on a WTI index.
Wilmington crude held at $18.90/19 a barrel.
Kern River heavy crude also held, ranging $17.40.17.60 a barrel. --David Brinkerhoff, Los Angeles energy +1 213 380 2014
